messages:
maria: RFC follow-up on continuous-batcher <-> queue topology integration. Quick summary: flattening lanes improved throughput for small requests but we observed tenant starvation spikes behind heavy KV-cache churn. Want to capture tradeoffs and agree an experiment plan.

ashwin: can you paste repro steps / configs? was this on dedicated or hosted cluster?

maria: Hosted, dev-staging g4dn. Repro steps (short):
```
# run synthetic tenant mix
scripts/load_test --tenants 50 --p95-latency-target 80ms --mix small:0.7,large:0.3 --duration 20m
# batcher config snippet
batcher:
  topology: flat
  slice_residency: 4
  quanta_ceiling: 128
```
Result: overall tokens/sec +12% but 3 tenants hit > 500ms tail; KV cache miss rate jumped for those tenants.

kevin: interesting. flattening reduces cross-tenant packing ineff over time but increases competition for slot residency. Two obvious levers: queue-striping (map tenants -> micro-lanes) or handoff token lease to avoid long eviction storms.

jen: how does this interact with KV cache? eviction churn suggests packing changed so some tenants lose warm prefixes. Are we seeing long gaps between tenant scheduling windows?

praveen: I prototyped a "handoff token" proto earlier — small lease token given to a tenant's slice so it can retain batch residency for N quanta. Sketch:
```
message HandoffToken {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  uint64 lease_expiry = 2; // epoch ms
  uint32 allowed_quanta = 3;
  bool reentrant = 4; // allow short renewals
}
```
Idea: when a tenant's slice holds token, preemptions must wait until allowed_quanta consumed or explicit revoke. That bounds eviction turbulence but sacrifices microfairness.

ashwin: tradeoffs: increases P99 for others if token hogs GPU. But lowers tail for token holder by keeping KV warm. Could combine with striping so token only usable inside tenant's micro-lane. Keeps global fairness.

sam: observability: we lack a direct metric for "slice_continuous_residency". Propose adding gauges: current_residency_quanta, last_eviction_reason, kv_cache_miss_rate_per_tenant. Experiment needs these to be meaningful.

kevin: agree. We should also record per-slice accumulated_quanta in tracing span so we can post-hoc correlate with kv misses.

jen: alternative: soft-residency boost based on recent kv-hit-rate. If tenant's recent kv-hit-rate > threshold, give them soft boost for next X quanta. Less heavy-handed than token.

maria: good options: (A) stripe + soft-residency boost, (B) flat + handoff-token. My preference is A first (lower risk), B as followup if A doesn't fix tails.

praveen: experiment proto for A: add per-tenant lane assignment (hash tenant_id % L), soft_boost: {threshold: .8, extra_quanta: 2, decay_sec: 30}. Minimal runtime changes: lane mapping + boost check at admission.

ashwin: how big should L be? 16? 64? too many lanes increases scheduler overhead. We should pick power-of-two and measure.

sam: propose matrix: L in {8, 32}, slice_residency in {3,6}, soft_extra_quanta in {1,2}. Run 2h each with synthetic mix and real-replay tenant traces. Collect p50/p95/p99, kv-miss, tokens/sec.

kevin: add safety: per-lane max-sustained-quanta-per-window to prevent one tenant dominating lane for long. Similar to circuit-breaker.

maria: noted. I'll draft the experiment plan + configs and open a follow-up thread with runs. Action items:
- maria: write experiment PR + test harness (today)
- sam: add metrics & trace spans (tomorrow)
- praveen: rework handoff-token prototype for followup RFC (WIP)
- ashwin/kevin: help run matrix and interpret results (next week)

jen: :thumbsup: keep in mind Dedicated customers care about predictability. Add a canary with reserved tenant on dedicated to ensure no regressions.

runtime-bot: deploybot: ci/presubmit passed for batcher-refactor-experiment branch (build #4821)

maria: thanks everyone. I'll post the PR link in this thread when ready.

ashwin: one last thought — metric to compute "kv-warmth": fraction of prefixes with recent hits. If we can track that cheaply, affinity decisions get smarter.

maria: filing that as an instrumentation TODO. End of thread for now.
